headline: Signs It Is Time to Call a Professional for Kitchen Flooring Replacement
articleBody:
A new kitchen floor is a major upgrade, and while laying floating planks in an open bedroom might seem straightforward, a kitchen presents unique structural and plumbing hurdles. Knowing when to hand the project over to experienced pros ensures your investment lasts.

Here are clear signals it is time to call a professional for your kitchen flooring:

- Your current floor has noticeable height differences: If your kitchen transitions unevenly into your dining area or living room, a professional can properly adjust subfloor heights and transitions.
- Dishwashers or ranges have tight vertical clearances: New tile or thick hardwood can raise the floor level, accidentally trapping built-in appliances beneath your fixed countertops.
- You suspect moisture issues in the subfloor: Soft spots around your sink, swollen baseboards, or damp slab conditions demand proper remediation, moisture testing, and heavy-duty vapor barriers.
- The subfloor requires structural leveling: Installing over an out-of-flat surface leads to hollow sounds, broken tile grout, or clicked plank seams coming apart under foot traffic.
- You want complex layouts or continuous layouts around islands: Cutting cleanly around fixed cabinetry, pantry corners, and kitchen islands requires precision and proper expansion gaps.

What to Do Next
If your project involves tricky subfloors, appliance height adjustments, or moisture testing, professional expertise prevents costly re-dos down the road.
